subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Energy transferred to a trophic level is 50,000 kJ per m2 per yr and that passed on to the next level is 5,000 kJ per m2 per yr. What is the percentage efficiency of transfer?
Compared with earlier seral stages, how does the climax community generally compare in biodiversity and stability?
questions.explain: The climax community is typically the most biodiverse and stable end point of a succession.

questions.q: A producer has a GPP of 20,000 kJ per m2 per yr and respiratory losses of 8,000 kJ per m2 per yr. What is its NPP?
questions.explain: NPP = GPP - respiration = 20,000 - 8,000 = 12,000 kJ per m2 per yr.

questions.q: Sexual selection can lead to the evolution of features (e.g. a peacock's tail) that reduce survival because such features:
options: Increase mating success enough to outweigh the survival cost
questions.explain: If a trait raises an individual's mating success more than it lowers survival, the allele still increases in frequency.

questions.q: Modern classification places organisms into three domains. These are:
questions.explain: The three-domain system divides life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based largely on rRNA sequence differences.

questions.q: In the mark-release-recapture method, the Lincoln index estimates population size N using which expression?
options: N = first marked + second sample - recaptured marked
N = recaptured marked / (first marked x second sample)
N = (first marked x second sample) / recaptured marked
questions.explain: Population = (number first marked x total in second sample) / number marked in the second sample.

questions.q: In a classic predator-prey relationship, why does the predator population peak shortly after the prey population peaks?
options: Predators reproduce before prey are available
Prey numbers never affect predator numbers
Abundant prey allows more predators to survive and reproduce, with a time lag
Predators cause prey numbers to rise
questions.explain: A peak in prey provides plentiful food, so predator numbers rise afterwards, lagging behind the prey peak.

questions.q: How does ploughing and draining waterlogged soil tend to affect the nitrogen available to crops?
options: It converts nitrate to nitrogen gas
It improves aeration, favouring nitrifying bacteria and reducing denitrification
questions.explain: Better aeration favours aerobic nitrifying bacteria and limits anaerobic denitrifiers, so more nitrate remains for plants.

questions.q: How does secondary succession differ from primary succession?
options: It involves no change in species over time
It begins on land that already has soil, e.g. after a fire
It never reaches a climax community
It begins on bare rock with no soil
questions.explain: Secondary succession starts where soil already exists, so it proceeds faster than primary succession.

questions.q: Which of the following is a density-dependent factor affecting population size?
options: Competition for food as the population grows
questions.explain: Competition intensifies as density rises, so its effect depends on population density, unlike abiotic events.

questions.q: Sympatric speciation differs from allopatric speciation because it occurs:
options: Without geographical separation, e.g. by behavioural or temporal isolation
Only after a geographical barrier forms
questions.explain: Sympatric speciation happens within the same geographical area through reproductive isolation mechanisms other than geography.

questions.q: How is gross primary productivity (GPP) best defined?
options: The energy remaining after respiratory losses
The biomass of all trophic levels combined
The total rate at which producers convert light energy into chemical energy
The energy lost as heat by consumers
questions.explain: GPP is the total chemical energy fixed by producers before any is lost in respiration.

questions.q: Human birth mass shows that very small and very large babies have higher mortality, while intermediate masses survive best. This illustrates:
questions.explain: Selection against both extremes in favour of the intermediate is stabilising selection.

questions.q: Which equation correctly expresses net primary productivity (NPP)?
questions.explain: NPP is the energy left for growth after the producers' respiratory losses are subtracted from GPP.

questions.q: Using the data above (q = 0.1), the frequency of heterozygous carriers (2pq) is:
The founder effect occurs when:
options: A large population is split equally by a barrier
A small group establishes a new population carrying only a subset of the original gene pool
questions.explain: A few founding individuals carry only part of the parent population's genetic variation, skewing allele frequencies in the new population.

questions.q: Stabilising selection acts to:
options: Favour both extremes against the mean
Favour the intermediate (mean) phenotype and reduce variation
questions.explain: Stabilising selection favours the mean phenotype, selecting against extremes and reducing variation.

questions.q: For the mark-release-recapture method to give a valid estimate, which assumption must hold?
options: Marking does not affect survival and marked individuals mix randomly with the population
questions.explain: The estimate assumes marks are harmless and that marked individuals redistribute randomly before the second sample.

questions.q: During primary succession, what is the key role of the pioneer species?
options: They form the stable climax community
They are the top predators of the food web
They colonise bare rock and begin soil formation
They prevent any further species from establishing
questions.explain: Pioneers such as lichens colonise inhospitable bare surfaces and start building soil for later species.

questions.q: When using random quadrats to estimate the abundance of a species in a large field, why must the quadrats be placed randomly?
options: To avoid bias so the sample fairly represents the whole area
questions.explain: Random placement avoids sampling bias, giving an estimate that fairly represents the whole study area.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prezygotic reproductive isolating mechanism?
options: Differences in courtship behaviour preventing mating
questions.explain: Behavioural (courtship) isolation prevents mating, acting before a zygote can form, so it is prezygotic.

questions.q: Which genus of bacteria fixes nitrogen within the root nodules of leguminous plants?
questions.explain: Rhizobium lives mutualistically in legume root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

questions.q: The maximum population size an environment can support sustainably is known as the:
questions.explain: Carrying capacity is the maximum population an ecosystem's resources can support over a long period.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of conversions during nitrification?
options: Nitrogen gas then ammonia then nitrate
questions.explain: Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonia to nitrite (Nitrosomonas) and then nitrite to nitrate (Nitrobacter).

questions.q: During succession, how does each community typically change the environment?
options: It makes conditions less suitable for itself but more suitable for the next community
It reduces biodiversity at every stage
questions.explain: Each stage alters the abiotic conditions, often making them less suitable for itself but enabling new species to colonise.

questions.q: Why is so little energy transferred between successive trophic levels?
options: All energy is converted to oxygen
Decomposers add energy at each level
Energy is lost through respiration, heat, and indigestible or uneaten material
questions.explain: Much energy is lost as heat in respiration and in material that is not eaten or not digested.

questions.q: Comparing the base sequence of DNA or amino acid sequences of proteins helps classification because more closely related species:
options: Show fewer differences in their base or amino acid sequences
questions.explain: Closely related species have had less time to accumulate sequence differences, so they are more similar.

questions.q: Which describes a density-independent factor affecting a population?
options: Disease spread in a crowded population
A severe frost killing organisms regardless of population size
questions.explain: A frost affects the same proportion of individuals whatever the density, so it is density-independent.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to evolution because:
options: Individuals change their genes during their lifetime to suit the environment
Alleles that increase survival and reproduction become more frequent over generations
questions.explain: Differential survival and reproduction of advantageous alleles increases their frequency in the gene pool over time.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which process converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or ammonium ions?
questions.explain: Nitrogen fixation, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium and Azotobacter, converts N2 into ammonia.
